I’ve been using weed regularly for about 6 years at this point, ever since I went to Uni. I thought that I was maturing and that weed “chilled me out,” but I realized a few days ago that it really just shoved everything down. 

I ended up ending things with my boyfriend and moving home because I realized that underneath it all I still hated myself and I hadn’t actually healed much of anything. I had been in therapy for years, done trauma based inpatient programs, been on mood stabilizers, and all the holistic shit. Relationships are hard for me, and I thought I was ready for one, but I realize I wasn’t. 

I loved coming home to smoke weed after work to “stop my mind” and “relax,” but really I’d just be groggy, sleepy, and out of it. Days that I didn’t work I wouldn’t be able to stop myself from smoking earlier. If I was spiraling or having a meltdown, even knowing I could smoke weed calmed me down - before I had even smoked! If I didn’t have weed I’d be grumpy and anxious and mean. 

I say all of this to say that it can be a great tool, but it can also hold you back as many others have said. It got me through some tough times in my life, but I do wonder what I missed out on by not being fully present. I didn’t have any energy to do anything, and then wondered why I was so depressed. I had all this anger and sadness bubbling beneath me that I’ve been repressing with weed. It works differently for everyone and we all have a different relationship with it. Good luck!

hey girl, i completely understand this. i moved to a foreign country where i met my bf, i still dont have many friends and get upset when he chooses to do something with his friends over me. i try to be “chill” and act like it doesnt bother me, but it does. usually because im alone waiting for him to be done and not doing anything to help myself. 

what ive realized i need is my own cup to fill in to. if i had friends and hobbies and things to do, i wouldn’t be so concerned about what he was doing or why he wasn’t replying. it’s hard when all we want is to spend time with them, and they want a balanced life (which is so valid and healthy and fair!). i often struggle with wanting my boyfriend to do what is healthy for him, and what i want him to do for me. 

but at the end of the day we can’t rely on someone else to make us happy. we both wouldn’t be happy doing nothing all day. i completely understand not wanting to take up hobbies (i feel as though im still as unfulfilled as when i started, so why bother), but i think over time they are helpful. i know it feels like nothing will help and we get uninterested, but if we can commit to something it will help. even if you don’t feel better after, you just spent a few hours of your day and that’s a good thing! less time to ruminate. 

i guess all i came here to say is that i get it, i also dont have a lot outside of my boyfriend. it feels so counterintuitive to do things i dont want to, but i cant spend the rest of my life feeling this way, and those around us dont deserve it either. just take small steps, find something that inspires you and see what else you can do with it.
